nodes.name: Pt islands electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Pt(111) modified by electrochemically deposited Pt islands, referred as Pt-islands/Pt(111). After 50 potential cycles between -0.3 V and +0.3 V, the STM images and the CV traces remain the same.
nodes.source_text: we used scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) to compare the atomic structures of Pt(111) and Pt(111) modified by electrochemically deposited Pt islands... After 50 potential cycles between -0.3 V and +0.3 V

nodes.name: Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition on Pt(111)
nodes.procedure: Pt(111) surfaces modified by electrodeposition of Ni-(hydroxide) clusters. The local symmetry, oxidation state of Ni atoms, and bond distances determined by in situ XAS. Ni(OH)₂ clusters exhibited hemisphere-like shapes with diameters ~8-10 nm and heights ~0.7 nm corresponding to two layers. VW-type growth observed.
nodes.source_text: we modified Pt(111)... by depositing Ni-(hydroxide clusters (38)... from the analysis of the x-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) and extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS)

nodes.name: Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition on Pt-islands/Pt(111)
nodes.procedure: Deposition of Ni(OH)₂ on a Pt(111) surface modified by ~0.2 monolayer (ML) of Pt islands. The clusters had approximately constant heights of ~0.8 nm but diameters ranging from 4 to 12 nm.
nodes.source_text: The STM image in Fig. 2A was acquired after deposition of Ni(OH)₂ on a Pt(111) surface modified by ~0.2 monolayer (ML) of Pt islands.

nodes.name: Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition on Pt(110)
nodes.procedure: Pt(110) single-crystal surface modified with Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.name: Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition on Pt-nano
nodes.procedure: Conventional Tanaka Kikinzoku Kogyo (TKK) catalysts (5-nm Pt catalyst) surface covered with Ni(OH)₂. Fractional coverage of Ni(OH)₂ was estimated to be ~15 to 20%.
nodes.source_text: we studied the conventional Tanaka Kikinzoku Kogyo (TKK) catalysts (5-nm Pt catalyst, Fig. 4C)... fractional coverage of Ni(OH)₂ was estimated to be ~15 to 20%
HER activities for Pt(111), Pt-islands/Pt(111), and Ni(OH)₂/Pt(111) surfaces in alkaline solution (a, b, and c, respectively)

in alkaline solution, relative to the corresponding pristine Pt(111) surface, the Pt-islands/Pt(111) surface is ∼5 to 6 times as active for the HER. Figure 1D also shows that in acid solution, the HER on the Pt-islands/Pt(111) electrode is improved by a factor of only ∼1.5

Although in the presence of Ni(OH)₂ clusters there are 35% fewer Pt sites available for the HER than on the bare Pt(111) substrate, the Ni(OH)₂/Pt(111) electrode is ∼7 times as active for the HER relative to Pt(111)

activity is further enhanced [by a factor of ∼8 relative to bare Pt(111)] on the Ni(OH)₂/Pt-island/Pt(111) surface; at 6mA/cm², the difference in overpotential between the HER in alkaline and acid solutions is reduced to only 100mV

Given that at the same overpotential (∼120mV) the current density obtained on the nanocatalysts is ∼8 times the current density on the most active extended surface

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂ clusters on Pt(111) show hemisphere-like shapes with diameters of 8-10 nm and heights of 0.7 nm corresponding to two layers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All Ni(OH)₂ clusters exhibited hemisphere-like shapes, with characteristic diameters of ∼8 to 10 nm and heights of ∼0.7 nm, the latter corresponding to two layers of Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: XAS analysis shows Ni-O bond distance of 2.05±0.01 Å, Ni-Ni bond distance of 3.08±0.01 Å, and Ni remains mostly in +2 valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: from the analysis of the x-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) and extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) of the XAS spectra ... we found Ni-O and Ni-Ni bond distances of 2.05±0.01 Å and 3.08±0.01 Å, and we also determined that Ni remains mostly in the +2 valence state

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES spectra for Ni(OH)₂ on Pt(111) show no shift in edge energy between HER (-0.1 V), Hupd (0.1 V), and near OER (1.2 V) compared to reference Ni(OH)₂ spectrum.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inset shows XANES spectra for Ni(OH)₂ on Pt(111) shown for three different potentials: HER (−0.1 V), Hupd (0.1 V), and near OER (1.2 V). Also shown is the reference spectrum for Ni(OH)₂. No shift in the edge energy in XANES spectra between HER and Hupd regions is observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂ clusters on Pt-islands/Pt(111) show ellipsoidal shapes with heights of 0.8 nm and diameters 4-12 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The clusters had approximately constant heights of ∼0.8 nm but diameters ranging from 4 to 12 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-nano catalysts show average particle size of 5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron micrograph image ... of Ni(OH)₂ free Pt-nano catalysts (TKK) with an average particle size of 5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ surface x-ray crystal truncation rod measurements confirm Ni(OH)₂/Pt surface morphologies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface morphologies of Ni(OH)₂/Pt(111) and Ni(OH)₂/Pt-islands/Pt(111) were probed by STM and in situ surface x-ray crystal truncation rod (CTR) measurements

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-islands/Pt(111) shows 2D Pt islands with diameters of 1-3 nm and monoatomic height (1 atomic layer).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the STM image of the islands shown in Fig. 1B, however, the Pt adatoms can be clearly resolved as 2D features with diameters of ∼1 to 3 nm and a height of 1 atomic layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂/Pt-islands/Pt(110) shows Ni(OH)₂ clusters randomly distributed on inherently rough Pt(110) surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STM image (50 nm by 50 nm) and CV trace for Ni(OH)₂/Pt-islands/Pt(110) single-crystal surface. STM image shows Ni(OH)₂ randomly distributed on inherently rough Pt(110).
